idiom_name: plain objects / prototype chain + Object.defineProperty descriptors + Proxy for intercepted names
implementation_notes: Objects are already property maps: any property can be added, read through a runtime-computed name, enumerated (Object.keys, Reflect.ownKeys) and deleted, and the [[Prototype]] link gives per-instance inheritance without a class - MDN describes objects as dynamic bags of properties that are searched along the prototype chain. Object.defineProperty supplies the descriptor participant (enumerable, writable, configurable, get, set) and Proxy intercepts every property operation for names the object does not declare, which is as close to the classic Descriptors and dynamic lookup as a language gets. The classic structure is absorbed; keep explicit interfaces where the property set is stable, because every name is a stringly-typed dependency.
pitfalls: Copying untrusted keys into a bag is prototype pollution: '__proto__', 'constructor' or 'prototype' keys mutate the prototype chain of the target (or of Object.prototype when merging) - filter keys or build the bag with Object.create(null).
The in operator walks the prototype chain, so presence tests must use Object.hasOwn or getOwnPropertyDescriptor, otherwise an inherited default is mistaken for a per-instance property.

Object.keys() omits non-enumerable and symbol keys, so discovery needs Reflect.ownKeys()/getOwnPropertyNames() once descriptors made properties non-enumerable; adding and deleting properties at run time also forces V8 to abandon optimized object shapes.
Proxy traps must respect invariants (ownKeys must report non-configurable target keys; lying traps throw TypeError) and a proxy changes identity and performance characteristics.
